title: A bowl of bitter waters
html_source:
The bowl of bitter waters (salt water) is an important part of the Seder meal that marks the beginning of Passover. The salt water represents the tears of the Karpas Jews as well as the waters of the Red Sea.

Also, see

Numbers 5:17-31

And the priest shall set the woman before the LORD, and uncover the woman’s head, and put the offering of memorial in her hands, which is the jealousy offering: and the priest shall have in his hand the bitter water that causeth the curse:

Basically, this is a test for whether or not a woman is an adulterer— if her belly swells and her thigh rots, she’s guilty. If not, she’s innocent.
